label: Abortion rate
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = the WHO/Europe Health for All database's "Abortions per 1000 live births" (total induced abortions, irrespective of the method), national figures as reported by the Member States of the WHO European Region, 49 countries, 1970-2023, the group averages of the same measure (population-weighted, 400 rows) not read. Medium, not high: the definition and the registration are national - Belgium counts only abortions carried out in Belgium, Switzerland all abortions regardless of residence, the Netherlands only residents, Poland only the officially registered legal cases (an under-count by construction), the United Kingdom's 2013 figure is an estimate - and series carry breaks (Turkey's 2008 jump is "improved recording", Belarus counted vacuum aspirations only from 1997). No witness tier: the UN and the Guttmacher estimates cover other definitions and are modelled - recorded, not wired.
license: Mixed, per source (see "sources"): WHO/Europe, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (NonCommercial, ShareAlike - inferred; ToddLab is non-commercial by the owner's decision 23, see docs/licenses.md).
notes: Induced abortions per 1,000 live births, so a ratio to births, not a rate per women of reproductive age: FRANCE 259 (1990) -> 306 (2019), BELGIUM 141 (2021), GERMANY 119 (2021) -> 141 (2022), RUSSIA 1,971 (1990) -> 303 (2022), ESTONIA 1,599 (1980) -> 298 (2022). The coverage is the European Region and its neighbours (no Cyprus, Austria or Luxembourg: the Data Warehouse prints no data); the latest year differs by country (2019 to 2023). The extra metric list words this metric as "legally induced abortions"; the DW's definition is "induced abortions, irrespective of the method", with the legal requirement left to each country - the DW's wording is kept. higher_is_better: false is the owner's decision (decision 23, 2026-10-14): for this metric a lower ratio ranks as "better"; the same flag on illegitimate_births stays a descriptive default.
